title: Unit economics: add rate limits + response caching for dashboard query APIs
author: Felix Schneider
release_notes: Internal-only: unit economics query endpoints now enforce rate limits and cache common responses to protect the warehouse and improve p95 latency for popular views.
description: Summary: Adds server-side caching and request rate limiting to the internal Unit Economics dashboard query APIs introduced in PR #19374. This is to (1) protect the warehouse/materialized views from repeated identical queries (especially top-N + timeseries defaults), (2) reduce load during Finance/exec review windows, and (3) improve dashboard responsiveness for common filters. Context: During dogfood we saw heavy burst traffic from the Console UI due to filter changes + auto-refresh + multiple panels firing in parallel. In the worst case, a single user interaction triggered 6-10 warehouse queries with identical group_by/filter payloads (only differing by panel). This PR implements deterministic cache keys and a small set of safe defaults that do not change correctness semantics (cached responses are bounded by short TTLs and include freshness metadata). Design notes: 1) Two cache profiles: "live" and "finance". Live is the default used by the dashboard UI (short TTL). Finance is intended for FP&A/QTD views where stability is preferred over second-to-second freshness (longer TTL), and is only enabled for specific endpoints/queries used in the KPI pack. 2) Cache keys are derived from the normalized query payload (filters + group_by + time_bucket + metric + sort + pagination) plus the caller's access scope (RBAC role + allowlisted feature flag). We explicitly do NOT include user_id in the key so a popular view can be reused across users, but we do include authz scope to avoid leaking data across roles. 3) Rate limiting is applied per user (preferred) or per IP (fallback), with separate buckets for (a) time series endpoints and (b) breakdown/top-N endpoints. We chose conservative defaults and added metrics/alerts to tune. 4) Adds response headers: X-Redwood-Cache (HIT/MISS/BYPASS), X-Redwood-Cache-TTL-Seconds, and X-Redwood-Data-As-Of (UTC timestamp) so UI and Finance can reason about freshness. Implementation details: - New middleware: economicsQueryGuard() which enforces (a) RBAC check (existing), (b) rate limit, (c) optional caching. - Caching uses our shared CacheService abstraction with Redis backend (same cluster used by Console), namespaced under unit_econ:query:v1. We cap cached payload size to 1.5MB and skip caching when the response exceeds the cap. - TTLs: live = 60s for time series and 120s for breakdown/top-N; finance = 15m for time series and 30m for breakdown/top-N. TTLs are configurable via flags: UNIT_ECON_CACHE_TTL_LIVE_SECONDS, UNIT_ECON_CACHE_TTL_FINANCE_SECONDS. - Cache bypass: request header X-Redwood-Bypass-Cache: true (allowlisted to internal admin role only) and query param bypass_cache=true (admin only). Bypass requests still write-through the cache unless bypass_write=true (admin only; intended for debugging). - Rate limits (initial): time series = 60 req/min/user, breakdown = 30 req/min/user, with burst=2x. Per-IP fallback is 30 req/min/ip for time series and 15 req/min/ip for breakdown. - Adds metrics: unit_econ_api_cache_hit_total{endpoint,profile}, unit_econ_api_cache_miss_total{endpoint,profile}, unit_econ_api_rl_block_total{endpoint,reason}, unit_econ_api_query_duration_ms{endpoint,warehouse=true/false}. - Adds structured logs for cache key + normalization hash (not the raw filters) to help debug "why didn't I hit cache" without leaking customer IDs. Security/privacy: The cache key derivation explicitly redacts/normalizes high-cardinality inputs and never logs raw customer identifiers. Responses remain aggregated; no per-customer breakdown is introduced here. The cache namespace is internal-only and protected by service credentials; however, we additionally include caller scope in the key to prevent any future role-based divergence from causing cross-scope reuse. Testing: - Unit tests for query normalization/canonicalization (ordering, default values, null vs omitted). - Integration tests for caching behavior: identical queries HIT, modified filter MISS, scope change MISS. - Integration tests for rate limiting (429) with deterministic clock. - Load test script (internal) for the default dashboard view shows ~72% cache hit after warmup; warehouse query count reduced ~4.6x for the same UI interaction pattern. Rollout plan: - Deploy behind feature flag UNIT_ECON_QUERY_GUARDS_ENABLED (default off). - Enable in staging for 24h, verify cache hit rate + 429 counts + no increase in error rate. - Gradually enable in prod for internal users (10% -> 50% -> 100%) coordinated with SRE (Sean) and Observability (Allison). - If Finance reports stale reads, switch Finance profile queries to bypass cache temporarily while we tune TTL or panel refresh behavior. Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Console UI: reduce redundant parallel calls by sharing panel queries client-side (Nora is tracking). - Add dedicated "finance view" toggle in UI (currently driven by endpoint usage + server-side profile selection). - Consider precomputing a small set of canonical views hourly (materialized cache) once we understand usage patterns.
commits: econ-api: add query guard middleware (rate limit + caching hooks)
econ-api: implement cache key normalization + scope-aware hashing
econ-api: add redis cache namespace + payload size caps
econ-api: enforce per-user/per-ip token bucket limits + 429 responses
econ-api: add cache and rate limit metrics + structured logs
tests: add integration tests for cache HIT/MISS and rate limit blocks
docs: add operator notes for tuning TTLs and investigating 429s
review_conversation: Chloe Martin (requested changes): Cache key should include the pagination cursor + sort order; otherwise top-N pages can collide. Also make sure defaults are applied before hashing so omitted fields don't create separate keys. Felix Schneider (author): Good call. Updated normalization to materialize defaults (time_bucket, sort_dir, limit) and include page_token in key material. Added tests for cursor collisions. Sean Gallagher (SRE): Rate limits look reasonable, but please add a distinct metric for blocks by bucket (timeseries vs breakdown) and emit X-RateLimit-* headers for troubleshooting. Felix: Added unit_econ_api_rl_block_total{bucket} and standard X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset-Seconds headers. Also updated 429 body to include bucket + retry_after_seconds. Allison Grant (Observability): Concern about caching "finance" views for 30m if the pipeline is behind; users might confuse staleness for cost improvement/regression. Can we expose an explicit data-as-of timestamp and show it in UI? Felix: Added X-Redwood-Data-As-Of and included data_as_of in JSON payload. Nora will surface it in the header bar (separate UI PR). Kaitlyn Nguyen (Security): Ensure cache key includes authz scope. Also do not allow bypass_cache for non-admin roles. Felix: Added scope hash (rbac role + feature flag state). bypass_cache and bypass_write are restricted to internal_admin. Mei Lin (Data Eng): Please cap payload size and avoid caching large time ranges that exceed view partitions; also prefer caching the post-aggregation response, not raw warehouse rows. Felix: Caching is only at the API response layer; added 1.5MB cap and skip caching when range > 90d unless finance profile explicitly requests it. Chloe Martin (approval): Looks good after changes; merging once CI is green.
deployment_notes: After merge: enable UNIT_ECON_QUERY_GUARDS_ENABLED in staging; watch unit_econ_api_cache_hit_total and unit_econ_api_rl_block_total for 24h. In prod, enable gradually; if 429s spike during dogfood, raise burst or coordinate with UI to reduce panel fanout. If Finance reports staleness concerns, switch finance-profile endpoints to bypass cache (admin-only) while tuning TTLs.
